title: Wake-on-LAN
desc: Send Wake-on-LAN magic packets to devices on your LAN to power them on remotely
empty: No devices yet. Add one, or import a Lucky config under "Settings → Backup & Migration"
broadcastPlaceholder: Leave empty for auto; separate multiple with commas, e.g. 192.168.1.255
checkHelp: Periodically opens a TCP connection to this address to check whether the device is online
shutdownConfirm: Shut this device down over SSH?
noConnections: No SSH connections in Web Terminal yet
untrustedHelp: Remote shutdown does not trust unknown hosts. Connect to this host once in Web Terminal to record its host key
shutdownHelp: Runs over the Web Terminal SSH connection. Windows needs the OpenSSH server enabled; on Linux, non-root users can use sudo -n shutdown -h now with passwordless sudo for that command.
bemfaTopicHelp: Requires Bemfa to be enabled. "Turn on" from a voice assistant wakes the device, "turn off" shuts it down (if remote shutdown is set up)
bemfaStep1: In the Bemfa console, create a topic under MQTT device cloud whose name ends with 001 (socket) or 006 (switch), e.g. pc001;
bemfaStep2: Enter the same topic on the device, then enter your private key here and enable it;
bemfaStep3: Link your Bemfa account in Mi Home (Xiao AI), Xiaodu or Google Home and sync devices to control them by voice.
bemfaUidPlaceholder: User private key from the Bemfa console
bemfaUidHelp: The private key works like an account credential; Gately only sends it over TLS to bemfa.com:9503
